blocks.title: Sample problem 6.9
blocks.problem: Calculate the heat of formation of sodium fluoride, which crystallizes in the sodium chloride lattice. The heat of atomization of Na(s) is 109 kJ/mol, half the bond energy of F₂(g) is 79 kJ/mol, the ionization energy of sodium atoms is 494 kJ/mol, the electron affinity of fluorine atoms is –328 kJ/mol, and the lattice energy is –939 kJ/mol.
steps: Solution: Values are given for all the quantities in the Born-Haber cycle, so we can apply Hess’ law:
ΔH°f = ΔH°latt + ΔH°at (Na) + ΔH°1i (Na) + ΔH°at (F₂) + ΔH°1ea (F)

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The result is the heat of formation of NaF: ΔH°f = –585 kJ mol⁻¹; the printed symbol is a bare Δ.

blocks.prompt: a) Draw Born-Haber cycle for sample problem 6.8.
blocks.explanation: (The Born-Haber cycle is that of Sample problem 6.9, NaF; see the Book correction.) At the bottom, Na(s) + ½F₂(g) (reactants). Going up: Na(s) → Na(g) (+109), Na(g) → Na⁺(g) + e⁻ (+494), ½F₂(g) → F(g) (+79). Then down: F(g) + e⁻ → F⁻(g) (−328), and Na⁺(g) + F⁻(g) → NaF(s) (−939). The total is −585 kJ mol⁻¹, which is ΔH°f for the direct route Na(s) + ½F₂(g) → NaF(s).

answer_figure.alt: Born-Haber cycle for sodium fluoride (not to scale). Bottom thick level Na(s) + ½F₂(g) (reactants). Upward arrows: ΔHat Na = +109, ΔHi Na = +494, ΔHat F (½ B.E. of F₂) = +79 kJ mol⁻¹; top level Na⁺(g) + e⁻ + F(g). Downward arrow ΔHea F = −328 to Na⁺(g) + F⁻(g), then a thick arrow, lattice energy −939, to NaF(s). Red arrow from the reactants to NaF(s): ΔHf = −585 kJ mol⁻¹.
answer_figure.caption: Answer diagram: Born-Haber cycle of sodium fluoride from the data of Sample problem 6.9 (not to scale)
answer_figure.long_description: This is a cycle like Figure 6.9 (NaCl), but with the data for NaF. From the reactants Na(s) + ½F₂(g), three steps go up: atomization of sodium (+109), ionisation of sodium (+494) and atomization of fluorine, i.e. half the bond energy of F₂ (+79 kJ mol⁻¹). Then F(g) gains an electron to form F⁻(g) (electron affinity −328), and the gaseous ions combine to form the NaF(s) crystal (lattice energy −939). The direct route, the red arrow, is the enthalpy of formation: −939 + 109 + 494 + 79 − 328 = −585 kJ mol⁻¹.

blocks.prompt: b) Calculate the heat of formation of lithium fluoride. The heat of atomization of Li(s) is 161 kJ/mol, half the bond energy of F₂(g) is 79 kJ/mol, the ionization energy of lithium atoms is 520 kJ/mol, the electron affinity of fluorine atoms is –328 kJ/mol, and the lattice energy is 1107 kJ/mol.
blocks.explanation: Taking the lattice energy as −1107 kJ/mol (energy is released; see the Book correction): ΔH°f = ΔH°latt + ΔH°at(Li) + IE(Li) + ΔH°at(F) + EA(F) = −1107 + 161 + 520 + 79 − 328 = −675 kJ mol⁻¹.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: (a) The Born-Haber cycle belongs to Sample problem 6.9 (formation of NaF); Sample problem 6.8 is the enthalpy cycle of solution of NaF. (b) A lattice energy as defined in 6.9.2 is released, so it is negative: –1107 kJ/mol, as Sample problem 6.9 uses –939 kJ/mol for NaF.
